description: This bar chart, from the paper "EssayBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese Essay Writing," illustrates the sample count distribution across four essay genres—Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository—with two distinct categories for each: "Open" (light blue bars) and "Cons." (pink bars), as indicated by the legend. The vertical y-axis, labeled "Sample Count," is scaled linearly from 0 to 120 in increments of 20, representing the number of samples in each category. The horizontal x-axis lists the four essay genres in the order presented. For each genre, two adjacent bars show the sample counts: for Argumentative, the "Open" category has 79 samples and the "Cons." category has 122; for Narrative, "Open" has 80 and "Cons." has 87; for Descriptive, "Open" has 68 and "Cons." has 100; and for Expository, "Open" has 62 and "Cons." has 130. The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the genres listed on the x-axis. The "Cons." bars are consistently taller than their corresponding "Open" bars across all genres, with the Expository genre showing the highest total sample count (130 for "Cons.") and the Argumentative genre showing the highest "Cons." count (122). The bars are not visually emphasized beyond their color coding and numerical labels.
